# Set Up

```{r}
#load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(emmeans)

typevector <- c(1, 2, 1, 4, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 3)

data <- data.frame(Type = factor(x = typevector, 
                                    levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4), 
                                    labels = c("alkaline, name brand",
                                                    "alkaline, store brand", 
                                                    "heavy duty, name brand", 
                                                    "heavy duty, store brand")
                                    ),
                  Time = c(602, 863, 529, 235, 534, 585, 743, 232, 282, 773, 840, 
                           255, 238, 200, 228, 215),
                  Cost = c(0.985, 0.935, 0.985, 0.495, 0.985, 0.985, 0.935, 0.520, 
                           0.495, 0.935, 0.935, 0.520, 0.495, 0.520, 0.495, 0.520),
                  CostPerUnit = c(611, 923, 537, 476, 542, 593, 794, 445, 569, 827,
                                  898, 490, 480, 384, 460, 413),
                  Order = seq(from = 1, to = 16, by = 1)
                  )
data <- data |>
                      mutate(Duty = case_when(
                        Type %in% c("alkaline, name brand", 
                                    "alkaline, store brand") ~ "alkaline",
                        Type %in% c("heavy duty, name brand", 
                                    "heavy duty, store brand") ~ "heavy duty",
                        TRUE ~ NA_character_),
                        Brand = case_when(
                          Type %in% c("alkaline, name brand", 
                                      "heavy duty, name brand") ~ "name",
                          Type %in% c("alkaline, store brand", 
                                      "heavy duty, store brand") ~ "store",
                          TRUE ~ NA_character_)
                          )
data
```

aov and anova

```{r}
# Use aov()  to fit the effects model with the response “Life per unit cost.” Use 
# emmeans and contrast to verify your estimates from problems 5 and 7.
# Fit the two-factor effects model with interaction
battery_model <- aov(CostPerUnit ~ Duty * Brand, data = data)

# Use aov and anova to fit the factorial effects model with the response “Life per # unit cost” and produce overall tests for the two main effects and the interaction
# effects.
anova(battery_model)
```

## Q1)

at alpha = 0.05 the interaction effect significant as Duty:Brand is 0.000558 which is less than the alpha value. this indicates that there is a significant interaction effect.

## Q2)

Because of the interaction effect is sign, a main effect can mask the true relationship and lead to misleading conclusions. Simple efffects would be better when interactive effects are sign.

## Q3)

The code below Estimates the marginal means of costperunit for each treatment combination. It displays the mean difference of duty on each level of brand. The p-value is testing if each sepereate cell mean is statistically different from zero.

```{r}
# emmeans() on duty/brand interactive effect
emmeans_inter <- emmeans(battery_model, ~ Duty | Brand)
emmeans_inter
```

## Q4)

```{r}
# contrast of emmeans of interaction effect
contrast_inter <- contrast(emmeans_inter, method = "pairwise")
contrast_inter
```

## Q5)

The function below is estmating the marginal means for each level of Duty regardless of brand. The p-value is testing if the marginal means are different from 0.

```{r}
# emmeans of main effect of Duty
emmeans_main <- emmeans(battery_model, ~ Duty)
emmeans_main
```

##  Q6)

```{r}
# contrast of the main effect of Duty
contrast_main <- contrast(emmeans_main, method = "pairwise")
contrast_main
```
